newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - GKN stung by $398 mln U.S. court award.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - GKN stung by $398 mln U.S. court award.

text.p: British vehicle components giant GKN was stung on Thursday by a U.S. court verdict that awarded U.S. franchisees of the group damages of $398 million.
The sum could be raised or cut at appeal, but GKN warned that if it lost again it could face damages of up to a maximum of $554 million.
"We are extremely surprised at the outcome which we believe to be wholly unreasonable and will appeal following delivery of the judgement," GKN said in a statement.

It added that it would make an appropriate provision as a charge in its 1996 accounts after considering the issues in the case, which was brought by franchisees of GKN's Meineke Discount Muffler Shops Inc in the United States.
"While this judgement represents a setback in the group's financial position it will have no effect on the board's decision in respect of the 1996 dividend," GKN added.
The company's shares fell sharply after the announcement, sliding 35-1/2 pence to 10.095 pounds by the close.
Analysts warned the shares could fall further if GKN failed to secure a reversal of the verdict or drastic cuts in damages.
One said the shares could fall by 6.6 percent from the last closing level of 1,045 pence per share, on the basis that $398 million in damages should be reflected in its market value.
Even if the damages award was not raised, the impact on cash reserves would be serious, he said.

He pointed out that GKN had 240-250 million pounds of free cash reserves which are unrelated to customer advance payments, "So if they had to pay the fine that would wipe out their cash balances and if they wanted to make an acquisition they would have to increase debt or make a rights issue," he said.
Another analyst saw shares falling 50 pence if the appeal by GKN is lost, but he was less pessimistic in his assessment.
He pointed out that "Yes, it is a shock for the market, but it is not significant to the operations of the company.
"If they lose there would be a large cash outflow and that could hit the value as a result of higher gearing. But it's a one-off scenario."
The case was filed in December 1993 in Charlotte, North Carolina over allegations that included breach of contract over Meineke advertising.
It arose from Meineke's administration of an advertising fund to which all Meineke franchisees contribute 10 percent of their weekly revenue.

According to the American Association of Franchisees & Dealers, this fund was established in 1982 by a Meineke corporate resolution which stated that Meineke should serve only as "conduit or agent" of the advertising contributions.
However, after Meineke in 1986 set up an in-house advertising agency, New Horizons Advertising, the plaintiffs claim the firm handled funds in a way that broke that agreement.
The franchisees have said they were seeking compensatory damages in excess of $100 million, as well as punitive damages, as a result of alleged actions by New Horizons.

The Charlotte district court has already said that GKN Plc should be a defendant in the case, It also allowed part of the claim to be made under the North Carolina Unfair Trade Practices Act, which carries a treble damages penalty.
